title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: our reprobation doctrine drives no one to despair who studies to avoid sin and obey — that study is surest election-mark; those not yet feeling it must use granted means, not despair
pass_a_gloss: Finally there is no one of mortals whom our sentence concerning reprobation can drive unto despair, if he study to avoid sin and to obey God; because this very study is in our judgment the most certain argument of election. Nor ought they to despair who do not yet feel such a study, but to use those media which have been granted them by God, by no means doubting but that God will exhibit his mercy unto those so acting.
pass_b_english: Finally: our doctrine of reprobation can drive no mortal to despair if he studies to avoid sin and obey God — for that very study is in our judgment the surest mark of election. Nor should those despair who do not yet feel such a study. They should use the means God has granted them, not doubting that God will show his mercy to those who so act.
source_text: Nemo denique mortalium est quem nostra sententia de reprobatione ad desperationem potest adigere, si studeat vitare peccatum et Deo obedire; quia hoc ipsum studium est nostro judicio certissimum electionis argumentum. Nec debent desperare, qui nondum sentiunt tale studium, sed iis mediis uti, quae sunt illis a Deo concessa, haud dubitantes quin Deus sic agentibus suam misericordiam sit exhibiturus.
